subject: blueprintSpitfire
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: Spitfire fighter plane.
Style: cyanotype blueprint.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Spitfire rendered in cyanotype blueprint style, using flat blues and white linework as a single TS module, keeping the model static and simple without extra joints.

I'm sketching the actual dimensions and proportions (fuselage length, wingspan, height) and figuring out a tail-down parked stance so the propeller and landing gear clear the ground. Then I'm mapping out the parts list: lofted fuselage, lathe-built cowling and spinner, extruded prop blades and elliptical wings with dihedral, tail surfaces, canopy, exhaust stacks, radiators, gear legs and wheels, cannons, and roundels, all rendered with deep Prussian blue fills and white panel lines, rivets, and ring details to sell the blueprint aesthetic.

I'm now plotting precise fuselage stations along the length axis with position, width, and height at each point to build the loft, adjusting the pitch so the nose sits higher and the tail lower to mimic the tail-wheel ground attitude, and placing the wing root height and landing gear strut length so the wheels meet the ground plane correctly.

Then I'm shaping the engine cowling and spinner separately using lathe profiles around the nose axis -- defining radius curves that bulge out behind the spinner then taper into the cowl, and sketching a shorter spinner cone profile just ahead of it -- before moving on to extrude the propeller blade outline.

Writing propeller blade geometry...

Now I'm setting up the wing extrusion, defining the span and chord axes to build out an elliptical planform.

Keeping thickness constant with chordwise taper is acceptable; I'm reconsidering dihedral by tilting the extrusion axis slightly instead, adjusting the x-vector to introduce a small vertical component while keeping it roughly orthogonal to the forward axis.

Now I'm working out the planform shape itself—modeling the Spitfire's elliptical wing with a root chord around 2.5 and tip chord near 0.8, generating leading and trailing edge points along the span using a chord function that tapers elliptically toward the tip.

I'm working out the wing outline points going counterclockwise from root to tip along the leading edge then back along the trailing edge, computing chord length via the elliptical taper formula, and adding dihedral so the tip rises above the root before placing the wing vertically near the fuselage.

Now I'm figuring out how to add aileron panel lines as a slightly raised, lighter-colored slab on the outer wing's trailing edge, using a helper function to interpolate between leading and trailing edge positions along the span.

Positioning the roundel discs on each wing, stacking concentric white and blue cylinders at decreasing radii, then working out the tilt direction to match the wing's dihedral normal for each side.

Now I'm setting up the tailplane geometry with a similar extruded outline at reduced scale, and starting the fin's cross-section orientation by computing its thickness vector from the side-view axes.

For the fin outline itself, I'm shaping the tall rounded rudder profile at the tail, with points sweeping back and up to roughly match a Spitfire's characteristic tail height, keeping the rudder as a separate lighter extrusion from the fixed fin.

For the canopy, I'm placing a scaled sphere bubble in light cyan at the cockpit position, then adding thin white frame lines using torus or cylinder shapes to simulate the canopy's dividing struts.

I'll keep the torus ring sizing close to the fuselage radius with slight scaling adjustments, then skip the dorsal fairing idea for simplicity. For details, I'm adding exhaust stacks as small tilted cylinders along the cowling sides in pale yellow-white, and planning wing-mounted cannon barrels next.

Now I'm positioning the cannon rods extending from the wing leading edge, sized and colored as thin white rods. I'm also placing elliptical radiator boxes under the wings with dark blue bodies and white intake lips, and starting to work out the landing gear leg positions beneath the wings.

Checking the wheel sits flush with the floor and the prop blades clear the ground near the spinner. For the tail wheel, I'm sizing a small strut and wheel near the rear fuselage, though the resulting height looks a bit tall compared to a real tail-dragger stance.

I'm reworking the fuselage profile to give it a proper tail-down attitude, tilting the longitudinal axis roughly 12 degrees and adjusting station heights from nose to tail accordingly. Then I'm checking that the wing root intersects the fuselage belly correctly, and positioning the tailplane and fin base to align with the new, lower tail height.

Now I'm defining the tail wheel strut and rod geometry, then settling on a cyanotype blueprint color palette with dark navy accents and pale line work, and planning to add panel-line detailing along the fuselage.

Still planning seam geometry...

I'll place about twelve rings slightly offset outward from the hull, interpolating station widths linearly to get the ellipse cross-section at each z. For the blueprint aesthetic, I'll skip grid decorations but add a white outline rod along the wing's leading edge and tip to echo the cyanotype line-art style.

Working out wing outline geometry...

Still defining tail geometry...

Still defining panel geometry...

I'm figuring out the roundel disc placement for the wing, computing chord width at that position to size the radius appropriately, then stacking thin cylinder layers for a slight relief effect oriented along the surface normal. I'm also planning matching roundel discs on the fuselage sides, interpolating the fuselage's half-width at that fore-aft position to size a smaller disc.

I'm considering adding squadron code letters and serial numbers to the fuselage using text textures on a plane, though it's a bit risky to get rendering right -- deciding to try it anyway.

I'll place the text just above the wing, around y=1.6, and skip adding glow effects except maybe a pale tint for the canopy. For fuselage seams, since lofting won't give clean sweep lines, I'll approximate them using torus rings and rods swept along interpolated point arrays for the dorsal ridge and side lines near the fuselage edges.

Writing placement and geometry logic...

Finishing the spinner profile and prop plane position, then adding white rings around the cowling, a small intake bump on top of the nose, and noting the fuselage axis tilt to leave mostly as-is.

Now I'm building the three propeller blades: positioning them radially around the nose center at 120-degree offsets, extruding a tapered blade outline for each, and adding a slim tip band near the end of each blade.

For color, I'm defining a palette of hull blues, dark navy, and pale glass tones, planning to use lighter accents for wing panels and a darker countershade for the fuselage underside.

Adding loft sectors and fuselage stations...

I'm also adding details like exhaust stacks, cannons, pitot tube, and an antenna mast rod positioned behind the cockpit, though I'll skip the connecting wire for now.

Working out the fin and rudder geometry — positioning the fin base relative to the fuselage tail height and tip coordinates, then starting the rudder outline points.

Defining wing geometry helpers...

Still working out panel geometry...

Still placing wheels, hubs, leg doors, and exhaust geometry...

Adding gun barrel stubs protruding from the wing leading edge for the cannons, plus a pitot tube under the left wing, and now computing radiator box positions using the wing chord geometry at that span station.
